subject: general
question: 'Kendriya Hindi Sansthan' has head office at which place as on July 2022?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Agra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The head office of Kendriya Hindi Sansthan is located in **Agra**.
 
• Kendriya Hindi Sansthan is an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Education, Government of India.
 
• It was established in 1960 with the objective of promoting and propagating Hindi as a common link language in India.
 
• The institute offers various courses and conducts research in Hindi language and literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kendriya Hindi Sansthan**

 
 
• Also known as the Central Institute of Hindi, it plays a crucial role in the development and promotion of Hindi language education across India and abroad.
 
• The institute runs various programs such as teaching Hindi to non-Hindi speakers, advanced research in Hindi, and training teachers in Hindi education.
 
• It collaborates with several international organizations and institutions to promote Hindi globally.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Education, Government of India**
 
 
• The Ministry of Education is responsible for the development of educational policies and administration of various educational institutions and initiatives in India.
 
• It oversees primary, secondary, and higher education and formulates policies to improve the quality of education in the country.
 
• One of the key objectives of the ministry is to promote the use of Hindi and other regional languages in education.
 
 
 
• **Hindi Language**
 
 
• Hindi is one of the official languages of India and is widely spoken across the country.
 
• The language has its roots in Sanskrit and has evolved over centuries, incorporating elements from various other languages.
 
• Efforts are constantly made by the Indian government and various organizations to promote the use and learning of Hindi both within and outside India.
